sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The graph is not semantically faithful: it creates an independently required ice-milling case and an independently required propulsion load case, without constraining the strength-evaluation load case to be the ice-milling sequence case being used. Enforce the required relationship/identity between these case nodes (for example, with a canonical path and an appropriate SHACL equality or nested constraint), while keeping loadCasePurpose on the loadCase owner. Also do not impose sh:minCount 1 on hasIceMillingSequenceCase unless the requirement independently requires every ship to have such a case; the wording is conditional on a propeller-milling-ice-block case. The positive propulsionLineStrengthEvaluationPurpose constraint correctly captures the intended use, and the stalling prohibition may remain as a non-stalling controlled-value constraint.

The identity constraint and conditional absence of sh:minCount are appropriate, but the candidate does not explicitly use the declared stallingAnalysisPurposeValue controlled term/evidence obligation. Add a canonical constraint on loadCasePurpose that rejects nltl:stallingAnalysisPurposeValue (for example, a property-level sh:not containing sh:hasValue nltl:stallingAnalysisPurposeValue) while retaining the required propulsionLineStrengthEvaluationPurpose value. Keep loadCasePurpose on the loadCase owner and preserve the existing equality between the ice-milling and propulsion load-case paths.
